subject: Post-call: SOC 2 & audit-log retention — clarifying questions
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@clearpay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: SOC 2 & audit-log retention — clarifying questions

Sara — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a set of clarifying questions so your security team can triage internally. Please let me know if any of these are out of scope or if you'd like a follow-up call with our SOC 2 lead (Soojin).

Top-level goals you stated
- Retention policy: ClearPay needs immutable audit logs for 12 months for transaction traces; 7 years for a small subset of regulatory events.
- Evidence: Your auditors will need access to event-level logs (read/write/delete) and renter/account mapping for a rolling 12-month window.
- Pen test: You prefer customer-facing pen test summary + remediation confirmation before go-live.

Pain / constraints we captured
- RTO/RPO: 1 hour for control-plane events affecting customer data flows.
- Limited connectivity: some ClearPay environments are air-gapped during monthly reconciliation periods.
- Contract: DPA draft needs to include explicit retention windows and a clause for tamper-evidence for audit logs.

Clarifying questions (please assign owners where helpful)
1) For the 7-year regulatory subset, can you share the filter criteria (event types, resources, or products) so we can scope storage and egress cost? (Michael?)
2) Will your auditors require direct read-only access to raw audit logs, or is a generated report/journal sufficient? If direct access, what format (S3, syslog, API)? (security@clearpay.com)
3) For air-gapped workflows, need to confirm if evidence can be delivered via signed artifacts (hash-signed archives) rather than live export. Prefer a quick checklist of which reconciliation windows are air-gapped.
4) Pen test: timeline + minimum scope (external network + app + infra), plus whether you require us to use third-party assessor or in-house results are OK.

Next steps I propose
- We’ll attach a short SOC 2 evidence summary and a sample of audit log export (anonymized) for your team to vet. (attached)
- Soojin — can you share our recommended retention/immutability architecture doc and a short note on tamper detection options?
- Sara/Michael — if you can confirm items 1–3 by end of week, Priyom will put together a cost estimate for the retention + retrieval SLA.

Regards,

Logan Wright
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf (summary of controls), sample-auditlog-preview.csv (anonymized sample), DPA-draft-clearpay.docx (redline-friendly)
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@clearpay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@clearpay.com>, security@clearpay.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: SOC 2 & audit-log retention — clarifying questions

Logan — thanks for the detailed recap, that’s very helpful. We’ll do internal triage but a few quick answers now:

1) 7-year subset: this applies to any transaction that modifies settlement instructions or customer KYC identifiers — Michael will share a concise list by tomorrow.
2) Auditors: they typically want direct read-only access to raw logs in S3 (gzip CSV or JSON). A synthetic report may not pass.
3) Air-gapped windows: monthly reconciliation runs are air-gapped for up to 48 hours; we can provide signed artifacts after each window.
4) Pen test: we require a third-party assessor and a remediation attestation. Target window is Q2 pre-prod readiness.

We also uploaded a short internal checklist to our shared Drive; I’ll paste the link once the security mailbox gives the OK.

—Sara
Sara Chen
Head of Compliance — ClearPay Inc.
sara.chen@clearpay.com

Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: SOC 2 & audit-log retention — clarifying questions

Hi Sara / Michael — looping in our security lead Soojin and including a couple concrete proposals to address the items you flagged.

Proposal highlights (high-level):
- Retention levels: 12 months (full event-level) + flagged-regulatory subset (7 years) stored in WORM-enabled S3 buckets with MFA-delete and object versioning.
- Auditor access: we can provide time-limited read-only S3 access with bucket policies scoped to auditor IPs and log exports in gzip JSON/CSV. We’ll include manifest files and checksum attributes for traceability.
- Air-gap support: signed, time-stamped tarballs (SHA256-signed) delivered to your secure intake SFTP or via AWS Snowball if required; we’ll document acceptance criteria.
- Pen test: we’re fine with third-party assessor; Redwood will provide a remediation wrap-up and attestation once fixes are applied.

Soojin — can you confirm the tamper-detection/immuability options and whether we need a change to our DPA language? I’ve attached a starter DPA redline as requested.

Action items and owners
- Michael (ClearPay): send filter list for 7-year subset (due 2028-02-15)
- Soojin (Redwood): confirm WORM + tamper options and short writeup (due 2028-02-16)
- Priyom (Redwood): produce retention cost estimate and S3 access pattern doc (due 2028-02-18)

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@clearpay.com>, Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@clearpay.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: SOC 2 & audit-log retention — clarifying questions

Hi Sara / Michael — quick technical confirmation and attachments.

Tamper-evidence options we recommend:
1) WORM buckets + Object Lock in Governance mode, combined with server-side encryption (KMS) and object checksums.
2) Periodic signed manifests: daily manifests signed with an HSM-backed key (we can provide public key) to prove chain-of-custody.
3) Append-only journaling in an internal Kafka topic with retention snapshots to S3 — useful for nearline audit queries.

For auditors needing direct S3 reads: we will provide a time-limited IAM role scoped to the auditor AWS account and an explanatory README with field mappings. If ClearPay requires alternative formats, we can also stream logs to a partner syslog endpoint.

Attachments: technical-tamper-options.pdf (short tech note), s3-access-playbook.md (access sequencing), sample-auditlog-preview.csv

Next steps: once Michael shares the 7-year filter list, I’ll finalize storage sizing assumptions and hand them to Priyom for the cost estimate. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you want to walk the tech proposals line-by-line.

—Soojin
